Prevention: The virus is transmitted through the use of diseased stem cuttings used for planting material and also by the whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci)
For non-resistant varieties avoid using stems obtained from stunted plants or from plants with mosaic on their leaves
In branching varieties of cassava, take planting material from the branches not from the main stem.
This may reduce the spread of the disease.
In non-branching cassava varieties, cuttings should be obtained from the upper half of the plant, not the lower stem
Monitoring: Monitor cassava fields regularly after sprouting through to plant maturity for symptoms such as stunted growth or distortion and mosaic patterns on the leaves
Monitor resistant varieties continuously to detect loss of resistance and ensure early replacement with new resistant cultivars
Direct Control: Rogue out young plants with mosaic leaves as this will reduce the spread of the disease
Prune defoliated branch terminals and mummified inflorescences during the growing season and remove spent fruit stalks during harvest
Restrictions: There are no chemical controls for this viral disease
